details.description: DeepSeek-Prover-V2 is DeepSeek AI's open-weight language model built specifically for automated formal theorem proving in the Lean 4 proof assistant. Fireworks AI, which hosts the exact model id used here, confirms it serves the larger 671-billion-parameter variant (DeepSeek also publishes a smaller 7-billion-parameter version), built on the DeepSeek-V3-Base architecture. It was trained with a recursive proof-search pipeline: DeepSeek-V3 decomposes theorems into subgoals that a 7B prover model solves, the assembled proofs and reasoning chains form cold-start data, and reinforcement learning with binary correctness feedback follows, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository. It is a mathematics/formal-verification specialist rather than a general-purpose chat model.
advantages: Achieves an 88.9% pass ratio on the MiniF2F-test formal-proof benchmark, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
Solves 49 of 658 problems on PutnamBench, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
Introduces ProverBench, a 325-problem benchmark spanning AIME competition problems and undergraduate mathematics, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
Released under DeepSeek's Model License with weights available for self-hosting, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
disadvantages: A specialist model for formal Lean 4 theorem proving, not a general-purpose chat or instruction-following model.
The 671-billion-parameter size requires substantial compute to self-host, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
use_cases: Automated formal theorem proving in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
Decomposing complex mathematical theorems into provable subgoals.
Benchmarking formal mathematical reasoning on competition-level and undergraduate problems.

notes: Catalog groups this under a single generic URI with no size suffix; Fireworks' own page for that exact model id confirms it serves the 671B variant and states a 163,840-token context window, matching catalog's max_input/max_output facts exactly, so this write-up describes the 671B model. PutnamBench is reported by DeepSeek as a raw count (49/658 problems), not a published percentage, so it is described in advantages rather than as an evaluations entry.
